messages:
olivia_l: Hi folks 3 I lost my physical insurance card before a trip and had to use an urgent care clinic in Austin (not in-network). They charged me $275 and the carrier denied the claim as 'no member ID provided' even though I paid. I have the receipt but not the card. Any guidance on submitting an appeal or getting reimbursed?

jamie_peopleops: Sorry that happened @olivia_l. Which plan do you have? If PPO you can often self-submit for reimbursement with proof of payment. If HMO it's trickier.

olivia_l: Redwood Plus PPO (enrolled Jan 2026). Provider receipt attached in email to myself. Denial message from carrier reads:
```
Claim#: 77890021
Status: DENIED
Reason: Missing member ID at time of service
Amount billed: $275
Patient responsibility: $275
```

ben_benefits: Ok. Steps I'd try: 1) Download digital ID from carrier portal (Member > ID card > Save PDF) and forward to the clinic so they can re-bill with the member ID. 2) If clinic won't re-bill, file an out-of-network claim/submission with the carrier including: itemized receipt, proof of payment (bank/cc), a short cover letter explaining lost card at time of service, and the member ID. 3) If claim still denied, ask for an appeal/exception citing emergency/urgent care and inability to present card.

mike_travelops: Also confirm whether the clinic can add the member ID retroactively to the claim. Many EHR systems let providers re-submit claims with corrected member data. Worth asking them to re-file with billing.

olivia_l: I spoke to the clinic billing and they said they could re-bill if I gave them the member ID and a signed form. I don't have the card but I can get the digital ID. How fast can we get a replacement card?

jamie_peopleops: I can trigger a replacement card request. Carrier usually issues a PDF within 24-48 hours. Want me to do that now and DM it to you?

olivia_l: Yes please, DM the PDF. Also if carrier requires an appeal letter, can People Ops draft a short template I can sign?

ben_benefits: I'll post a template here you can copy and sign.

To: Claims Department
Re: Claim #77890021 (Service Date: 2026-03-18)
I, Olivia L., was seen at Austin Urgent Care on 2026-03-18 for acute symptoms. My insurance card was misplaced at time of service and could not be presented. I have attached the itemized invoice showing payment in full. Please accept this documentation and reprocess the claim under my membership (Member ID: XXXXXXXX).
Sincerely,
Olivia L.

finance_bot: [automated] If you prefer an advance reimbursement while the carrier processes the claim, Finance can do a temporary payout against receipts. Upload the receipt to Expensify and tag it "health-advance"; @ryan_finance will review.

carrier_bot: [automated] Carrier claim tips: For urgent/emergency services, please include clinical notes and discharge summary if available. Appeals typically resolved within 30-60 days. Link: https://carrier.example/appeals

olivia_l: Thanks everyone. @jamie_peopleops please DM the PDF. @ben_benefits I'll use your appeal template and ask the clinic to re-bill first. Will request advance from Finance if re-bill takes too long. I'll post updates here once carrier replies. :+1:
